_about: Business-function facet — WHOSE WORK inside the organisation the deployment changes. Names are chosen so the axes cannot blur: finance-accounting not 'finance', production-operations not 'manufacturing', legal-risk-compliance not 'legal', training-enablement not 'education'. 19 entries: 10 priority, 8 standard, 1 record_only. There is deliberately NO bare 'operations' value (decision V3).

entries.definition: The function that answers and resolves customer requests: contact centres, help desks, service teams, field service.
exclusions: an internal IT help desk (that is it-infrastructure)
sales enquiries handled by sellers (that is sales)
entries.disambiguation: The function is who does the work. The customer-facing nature of the AI itself is a use-case question (customer-interaction).

entries.definition: The function that creates demand and manages brand, campaigns, content and customer communications.
exclusions: product management (that is rnd-product-development)
sales outreach owned by sellers (that is sales)

entries.definition: The function that sells: prospecting, qualification, proposals, quoting, account management, revenue operations.
exclusions: marketing campaigns (that is marketing)
post-sale support (that is customer-service-support)

entries.definition: The function that hires, onboards, develops and administers people: recruiting, HR operations, payroll, employee relations.
exclusions: running employee upskilling programmes (that is training-enablement)
workplace facilities (that is facilities-workplace)
entries.disambiguation: HR owns the employment relationship; training-enablement owns the learning programme.

entries.definition: The function that plans, records and controls money inside any organisation: FP&A, budgeting, invoicing, accounts payable and receivable, close, tax, internal audit of financial records.
exclusions: being a bank, insurer or fintech (that is the financial-services-insurance INDUSTRY)
entries.disambiguation: Deliberately named finance-accounting, not 'finance', so it cannot be confused with the financial-services industry. Both may apply when each is independently evidenced.

entries.definition: The function responsible for legal work, contracts, governance, audit, regulatory compliance and enterprise NON-SECURITY risk.
exclusions: security operations, threat and vulnerability work (that is information-security)
being a law firm (that is the professional-services INDUSTRY)
entries.disambiguation: Renamed from legal-compliance by decision V2. Coexists deliberately with the risk-fraud-compliance USE CASE: this value is who does the work; that one is what the AI solves. A bank's fraud model built by its compliance team carries both.

entries.definition: The function that plans and runs the flow of goods: demand and supply planning, inventory, warehousing, distribution, logistics execution.
exclusions: supplier selection and negotiation (that is procurement-sourcing)
the production line itself (that is production-operations)
generic 'business operations' prose
entries.disambiguation: One of the two concrete operations functions. Decision V3: there is NO bare 'operations' slug — generic phrasing such as 'improving business operations' assigns neither this nor production-operations, and the term goes to unresolved[].

entries.definition: The function that runs production or service delivery: line operation, process control, quality, maintenance, throughput and yield — in ANY industry.
exclusions: being a manufacturer (that is the manufacturing-industrial INDUSTRY)
moving finished goods (that is supply-chain-operations)
generic 'business operations' prose
entries.disambiguation: One of the two concrete operations functions (decision V3). A pharma company optimising a line is healthcare-life-sciences + production-operations.

entries.definition: The function that captures, curates, governs and makes findable an organisation's internal knowledge: documentation, policies, wikis, expertise directories.
exclusions: numeric reporting and dashboards (that is data-analytics)
the retrieval capability itself (that is the search-retrieval USE CASE)
entries.disambiguation: Added by decision V1: nothing covered internal knowledge capture as a FUNCTION — data-analytics is about numbers, and search-retrieval is a use-case type describing capability, not ownership.

entries.definition: The function that sets direction and allocates resources: executive leadership, corporate strategy, transformation offices, portfolio management, M&A.
exclusions: day-to-day decisions inside another function
the decision-support USE CASE
entries.disambiguation: The function is who owns the decision; decision-support is what the AI does for it.

entries.definition: The function that selects suppliers and buys: sourcing, tendering, negotiation, supplier management, spend control.
exclusions: moving and storing the goods once bought (that is supply-chain-operations)

entries.definition: The function that researches and develops what the organisation sells: product management, design, engineering research, formulation, testing.
exclusions: writing production software (that is software-engineering)
marketing a finished product (that is marketing)

entries.definition: The function that builds and maintains software: developers, QA, release engineering, developer platforms.
exclusions: running servers and networks (that is it-infrastructure)
being a software company (that is the technology-software INDUSTRY)
entries.disambiguation: Against the code-generation USE CASE: this value is who does the work; that one is what the AI produces.

entries.definition: The function that runs the technology estate: infrastructure, cloud operations, networks, endpoints, service management, internal IT support.
exclusions: writing product software (that is software-engineering)
security operations (that is information-security)

entries.definition: The security function, narrowly scoped: SOC and threat operations, vulnerability management, security monitoring, incident response, and access and identity security.
exclusions: contract review, audit and regulatory compliance work (that is legal-risk-compliance)
enterprise non-security risk
general IT operations (that is it-infrastructure)
entries.disambiguation: Renamed from security-risk by decision V2 and narrowed. Leaving 'risk' in both slug names would reintroduce exactly the axis blur this vocabulary exists to prevent.

entries.definition: The function that owns data and reporting: data engineering, data platforms, governance, business intelligence teams, analysts.
exclusions: capturing and curating documents and know-how (that is knowledge-management)
the analysis capability itself (that is the data-analysis-bi USE CASE)
entries.disambiguation: Against data-analysis-bi (use case): this value is the team that owns data; that one is what the AI does with it.

entries.definition: The function that upskills employees and partners: learning and development, sales enablement, certification and internal academies.
exclusions: being a school or university (that is the education-research INDUSTRY)
AI that teaches (that is the training-education USE CASE)
entries.disambiguation: Named a near-miss pair in the ambiguity tests with the training-education use case: this is running employee upskilling; that is AI that teaches.

entries.definition: The function that runs physical workplaces: facilities management, real-estate operations for own use, workplace services, health and safety.
exclusions: a property business (that is the real-estate-construction INDUSTRY)
production plant maintenance (that is production-operations)

entries.definition: The source discusses which part of the organisation is involved but supports no vocabulary value — the function cannot be placed from the evidence available.
exclusions: an axis that does not apply at all (record not_applicable in unresolved[])
entries.disambiguation: The single sentinel shared by all three axes, and the only slug exempt from cross-axis disjointness.
